sources.quote: Statistics Canada's alcohol sales tables show per capita volumes falling for several consecutive years
sources.title: The Daily — Control and sale of alcoholic beverages and cannabis, April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025
sources.evidence: On a volume basis, sales of alcohol declined by 3.0% to 2,898 million litres in 2024/2025, marking the fourth consecutive year volume sales have declined. Beer sales declined 3.8% to 1,876 million litres, marking the ninth consecutive annual decline in beer sales by volume. Canadians of legal drinking age purchased the equivalent of 8.0 standard alcoholic beverages per week in 2024/2025, down from 8.7 the previous fiscal year and 9.7 a decade ago.

sources.quote: Licensed convenience stores could sell beer, cider, wine and ready to drink products from September 2024, and grocery and big box stores followed by that October, while spirits stayed with the LCBO
sources.title: Alcohol sales in retail stores | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: After September 5, 2024, all eligible convenience stores were able to sell beer, cider, wine and ready-to-drink alcoholic beverages. After October 31, 2024, all eligible grocery and big-box grocery stores were able to sell beer, cider, wine and ready-to-drink beverages, including in large pack sizes. Within the expanded marketplace, the LCBO network will be the only retailer where spirits such as vodka, gin and whisky will be sold.

sources.quote: at least 20 per cent of beer containers on display from small breweries, 20 per cent of ready to drink containers and 10 per cent of wine containers
sources.publisher: Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO)
sources.title: Section 2: Regulatory requirements for licensees | Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
sources.evidence: At least 20% of the containers of beer on display are containers of beer produced by small breweries. At least 20% of the containers of ready-to-drink beverages on display are containers of ready-to-drink beverages produced by small breweries, small distilleries or small wineries. At least 10% of the containers of wine, excluding cider, on display are containers of wine produced by small wineries.

sources.quote: extending the two per cent cap on the annual excise duty inflation adjustment and the 50 per cent cut in excise duty on the first 15,000 hectolitres of beer brewed in Canada
sources.title: Government extends excise duty relief, provides direct support to Canadian breweries, distilleries and wine makers - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Effective April 1, 2026, the government announced a two-year extension of alcohol excise duty relief: the annual inflation adjustment on beer, spirit, and wine excise duties will remain capped at two per cent, and the excise duty rate on the first 15,000 hectolitres of beer brewed in Canada will remain cut by half. Together, these two measures are expected to provide more than $30 million in total relief through to 2028.

sources.quote: which have paid excise on Canadian wine since the 2022 repeal of the exemption
sources.title: EDN75 Repeal of Excise Duty Exemption for 100% Canadian Wine - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Budget 2022 proposed to repeal the 100% Canadian wine excise duty exemption, with the measure coming into force on June 30, 2022. The prior exemption for wine produced in Canada from 100% Canadian agricultural or plant product grown in Canada ended on June 30, 2022; 100% Canadian wine made from honey or apples remains not subject to excise duty.

sources.quote: Platform age gating follows the provincial minimum drinking age, 18 in Alberta, Manitoba and Quebec and 19 elsewhere
sources.publisher: Canadian Centre on Substance Use and Addiction
sources.title: The Impact and Effectiveness of Minimum Legal Drinking Age Legislation in Canada | Canadian Centre on Substance Use and Addiction
sources.evidence: The minimum legal drinking age has been set at 18 years for Alberta, Quebec and Manitoba, and at 19 years for all other Canadian provinces and territories.

sources.quote: The code bars associating alcohol with social, sexual or professional success
sources.title: Code for broadcast advertising of alcoholic beverages | CRTC
sources.evidence: The code prohibits advertisements from implying directly or indirectly that social acceptance, social status, personal success, or business or athletic achievement may be acquired, enhanced or reinforced through consumption of the product, and from implying that the presence or consumption of alcohol is in any way essential to the enjoyment of an activity or an event.

sources.quote: Quebec's Regie des alcools, des courses et des jeux applies the Loi sur les infractions en matiere de boissons alcooliques and its promotion regulation
sources.publisher: Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (Québec)
sources.title: Faire de la promotion et de la publicité sur des boissons alcooliques
sources.evidence: Permit holders must comply with the Regulation on the promotion, advertising and educational programs in respect of alcoholic beverages. A permit holder for on-premise consumption cannot, at any time, offer or grant a discount on the regular price of alcoholic beverages, and cannot announce free alcoholic beverage consumption in advertising. A manufacturer who intends to broadcast or have advertising for alcoholic beverages broadcast must first have it approved by the Régie.
